Titans' Cam Ward is one loss away from making bleak NFL history
item.description: Titans' Cam Ward is one loss away from making bleak NFL history originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans are not having a good 2026 NFL season. Cam Ward has shown some promise this year, which has been encouraging, but their defense is horrible, and the team has a 1-9 record. With how poorly the Titans have played, it shouldn't be a surprise that Ward has made some NFL history no player wants to set. But heading into Week 12 against the Jacksonville Jaguars , Ward is on the cusp of some all-time horrible history. As ESPN Research highlighted , if Ward loses to the Jaguars in Week 12, then he will have broken the record for most losses by a quarterback in their first two NFL seasons since at least 1950. Cam Ward is one loss away from breaking NFL QB losing record "Titans QB Cam Ward is 4-23 as a starting QB," ESPN Research shared. "A 24th loss would break a tie for the most losses by a starting QB in his first two NFL seasons since 1950." Ward has only three wins in his NFL career, with his 23 losses over the past two years being an incomprehensible stretch of losing for the second-year QB out of Miami. At 1-9 this year, with their lone win coming against the Indianapolis Colts back in Week 6, Ward has quite the history of losing in his career. Through two years and 26 games played, he has 23 losses. One more loss, and he'll have the most losses by any quarterback ever through the first two NFL seasons. With the Jaguars, the current AFC South division leaders, on the schedule for Week 12, it wouldn't be a surprise for the Titans to lose this week and give Ward the record. MORE : Dak Prescott makes Cowboys history as Jerry Jones delivers telling reaction after Titans blowout This isn't the kind of record anyone wants to set, but the Jaguars present a big challenge for Ward and Tennessee this week. But even if they beat the Jaguars, Ward is still likely to break this record if he's healthy. After facing Jacksonville in Week 12, the Titans have the following opponents on their schedule: Washington Commanders , Detroit Lions , Colts, Las Vegas Raiders , Pittsburgh Steelers , and Houston Texans . While the Titans could potentially beat the Colts, Raiders, Steelers, and Texans, the Commanders are playing well lately, and the Lions are one of the best teams in the league. Seeing this Titans team win out this year would be maybe the biggest surprise the NFL has seen in a long time. Ward hasn't broken this record, but it is very likely he'll break it at some point this year. Unfortunately, all signs point to Ward joining the NFL history books in his sophomore season, but for the wrong reasons. One more loss, and he'll have the most losses a QB has ever had through their first two NFL seasons since 1950. item.description: Ordine slams Milan’s Estupiñán: ‘Terror all over his face’ Franco Ordine has launched a stinging attack on Pervis Estupiñán, claiming the Milan full-back is “terrified” of making mistakes in a Rossoneri shirt. In the Corriere dello Sport, with quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb , the veteran journalist used his regular column to look at Milan’s individual performances after Thursday’s 4-2 comeback win at Olympiacos. “Estupiñán now has a complex about wearing the Milan shirt. Just look at his face when the cameras zoom in on him in key moments: he has terror painted all over it,” Ordine wrote. “And if you’re terrified of making mistakes, it’s mathematically certain that you’ll make them.” Estupiñán started in Piraeus, where Milan were missing Davide Bartesaghi through injury. item.title: Flavio Briatore Got Rich on Benetton’s US Boom—Then Saw His First Grand Prix in 1988
item.description: Flavio Briatore was already wealthy from Benetton’s American franchise boom when he watched his first Formula 1 race, in Adelaide in November 1988. He went on to run a championship-winning team, get banned from the sport and come back. But the money came first, and it came from selling sweaters in America. How Benetton’s American Boom Made Briatore Rich Benetton, the Italian knitwear brand, opened its first five stores in the United States in 1979. Within about three years, Briatore was the Benetton Group’s main representative in the country. His job was to sign up the people who opened the shops. By one account, he took a percentage of every deal he arranged , and he did a lot of them. Benetton had 800 stores in North America by 1988. The boom didn’t last. Store owners complained about rival Benetton shops opening nearby, and the North American count later fell to about 200. By then, Briatore had moved on. Luciano Benetton, whose family had put its name on an F1 team in 1986, sent him to the Australian Grand Prix. Briatore had said he had no interest in the sport. After that race, he was made commercial director of Benetton Formula. He didn’t stay on the commercial side for long. Briatore pushed out the old management and ended up running the whole team. In 1991, he signed a 22-year-old Michael Schumacher after just one race for Jordan. Flavio Briatore (right) with Tom Walkinshaw at the 1993 British Grand Prix. Image Credit: Martin Lee / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0) From Schumacher’s Titles to Alpine Schumacher won the drivers’ championship for Benetton in 1994 and 1995, and the team took the 1995 constructors’ title. Briatore was replaced as team boss in 1997 and sold his shares. By his own account, the team wasn’t worth much by today’s standards. “I sold my share in Benetton, and the value of the team was $80million,” he told The Race this year. He put the same team’s value now at $3.5 billion to $4 billion. He came back when Renault bought the team, which raced as Renault from 2002. Fernando Alonso won the drivers’ title in 2005 and 2006, and Renault took the constructors’ crown both years. Then came Singapore. In September 2009, the FIA banned Briatore indefinitely after finding that Nelson Piquet Jr. had crashed on purpose in the 2008 Singapore Grand Prix to help Alonso win. In January 2010, a Paris court overturned the ban, ruling the FIA’s process had been flawed without ruling on the crash itself. Away from racing, he had already built a second business. Briatore started the Billionaire brand of nightclubs and fashion in 1998. He returned to Enstone, now home to Alpine, as an executive advisor in 2024. When team principal Oliver Oakes resigned in May 2025, Briatore took on his duties. His official title is still executive advisor, but he runs the team.

item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Bochum sink travel-sick Darmstadt with late goals
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Bochum sink travel-sick Darmstadt with late goals Bochum scored two late goals against Darmstadt to secure back-to-back home wins in 2. Bundesliga. The visitors lost all of their first six away games in the division. Both sides struggled for goals so far this season, and that was visible from the lack of clear-cut chances for the large part of the game. The hosts had the best opportunity of the first 45 minutes when the right fullback Klaiber hit the crossbar with a solo effort. Timo Horn was called into action late in the half as the ex-Köln shot-stopper made a couple of decent stops. The returnee Marcel Schuhen made his first save of the game early after the restart to deny Koji Miyoshi. The two goalkeepers continued on their excellent form by stopping Christian Rasmussen and Milan Smit from breaking the deadlock. When the deciding goal finally came, Schuhen was well beaten, however. Philipp Hofmann scored yet another headed goal from an inviting cross by substitute Berkan Taz. The former Karlsruhe man is only a goal shy of the top of the scoring chart at the age of 33. He also helped Uwe Rösler's side reach the Round of 16 in the DFB-Pokal with goals against his former club Greuther Fürth and Mainz. Darmstadt searched for a late equalizer as Schuhen joined to attack a set-piece opportunity, but that led to the second goal in the last action of the game. Taz finally grabbed his first Bochum goal with an open goal at his mercy in what was an exciting finish to a lifeless encounter for the most part. Darmstadt are still waiting for their first point away from home after competing for promotion the previous campaign. Bochum will host Augsburg on Wednesday in the DFB-Pokal before their last away game of the year next weekend in Nürnberg. Rösler's men momentarily climbed to eighth, while Darmstadt will spend another week in the relegation zone. Florian Kohfeldt's troops face Bundesliga's basement club Borussia Mönchengladbach in the DFB-Pokal Round of 16 tie.

item.title: White Sox Ignore Miguel Vargas Amid All-Star Form
item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images Miguel Vargas just put up an All-Star season, but the White Sox have not made a single move to extend his contract. While other clubs are locking up their core, Chicago seems content to wait. The delay comes right as Vargas becomes arbitration eligible. According to MLB Trade Rumors , a long-term deal does not appear to be on the White Sox’s radar at all. Timing the Lockout The front office has a clear reason for holding off, even if it feels risky to fans. Contract extensions are typically not discussed or finalized by clubs until the offseason concludes. James Fegan of the Chicago Sun-Times observes that the White Sox seem focused on outside acquisitions prior to the lockout instead of retaining internal talent. Since Vargas has three years of team control left, there is no urgent need to secure him right away. He is set to hit free agency following the 2029 season, which gives the organization plenty of time. For the infielder’s initial arbitration hearing, MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz estimated a $5.4 million salary. That number reflects his recent performance, yet the team remains quiet on a bigger commitment. Vargas Stays Focused The player himself has taken the high road despite the lack of official talks. Vargas suggested to James Fegan that talks between the two parties have apparently not started yet. Vargas stated: “Contracts or anything like that, I don’t want it to be a distraction for me. I’m very excited for what is coming for me and my future on the South Side. Hopefully I can stay there for many more years.” The player, aware his worth is rising, has taken a stance. Before being traded to the White Sox in a three-team deal, Vargas was a top prospect within the Dodgers’ farm system. The White Sox have not discussed an extension with Miguel Vargas, even though he had a breakout year.

item.title: Unusual Mikey Moore loan clause could save Cologne €1.5m
item.description: Unusual Mikey Moore loan clause could save Cologne €1.5m FC Cologne could end up paying virtually nothing in loan fees for Tottenham Hotspur attacker Mikey Moore thanks to an unusual clause in the 19-year-old’s agreement. According to a report appearing in the Wednesday print edition of Sport Bild , the Bundesliga club’s financial obligations decrease considerably depending on how frequently the English youngster features for René Wagner’s team. Moore’s season-long loan could theoretically cost Cologne as much as €1.5 million in loan fees. The agreement nevertheless contains a provision that reduces the fee with each qualifying appearance. Should Moore make 28 competitive appearances featuring at least 45 minutes on the pitch, the payment to Tottenham would drop to its lowest possible level. Cologne would then effectively be responsible only for the player’s wages. As of Wednesday, November 25, Moore had already accumulated eight appearances meeting the required playing-time threshold. Tottenham retain long-term control over Mikey Moore’s future The arrangement provides an obvious incentive for Cologne to continue giving Moore regular playing time, while Tottenham stand to benefit from the youngster gaining valuable Bundesliga experience. Cologne did not negotiate a purchase option as part of the agreement. Tottenham reportedly intend to incorporate the England youth international into their first-team plans for the 2027/28 campaign. The latest revelations also offer additional context to recent speculation concerning a possible premature termination of Moore’s loan . Cologne sporting director Thomas Kessler and head coach René Wagner have consistently emphasized their confidence in the youngster despite his initial difficulties adapting to German football. That patience finally began to pay dividends last Friday when Moore scored his first Bundesliga goal in Cologne’s impressive 1-1 draw against Bayern Munich. The teenager rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig after combining with Said El Mala to give the visitors an early lead. Moore subsequently spoke of his relief at ending his wait for a Bundesliga goal , while El Mala expressed optimism about the pair’s developing attacking partnership . With Moore showing signs of improvement, the financial structure of his loan offers Cologne another reason to continue investing in his development. Tottenham, meanwhile, stand to regain a more experienced player next summer without having surrendered control over his long-term future. GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: SMAT: Shreyas Iyer to turn out for Mumbai in super league; SKY to continue as captain
item.description: MUMBAI: In a big boost to Mumbai, India's T20 captain Shreyas Iyer will join the team for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Super League matches in Nagpur, TOI has exclusively learnt. However, India's 2026 T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav, who led Mumbai in the league stage, will continue as the Mumbai captain for the Super League. In fact, with all-rounders Suryansh Shedge (it's understood that Shedge will be available from the second match) and Tanush Kotian also set to be available after India A's campaign in the Rising Stars Asia Cup in Doha ended on Thursday with their defeat against Sri Lanka A in the semi-finals, Mumbai will be at full strength for the Super League stage of the SMAT. Under Surya's captaincy, Mumbai remained unbeaten in the league phase, winning six out of their seven matches in Kolkata to collect 26 points, while the seventh game was washed out. With 214 runs in six matches at 53.50 and a strike rate of 230, including two fifties, SKY was Mumbai's second-highest run-getter and showed signs of returning to form. Iyer last featured in the white-ball series against New Zealand in October, comprising five T20Is followed by five ODIs, and did not enjoy great form. He scored 126 runs in five T20Is at 25.20, with a strike rate of 151.80, and just 86 runs in the ODIs at 16.75, without scoring a fifty. The 31-year-old will thus get to play and get some runs under his belt in three, and possibly four if Mumbai make it to the final, matches in the SMAT Super League stage before turning out for India in the three-match home ODI series against Sri Lanka, starting December 13 in Visakhapatnam. He is India's ODI vice-captain. Kotian played just one match, against Sri Lanka in the semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars, in which he scored 28 and conceded 48 runs without taking a wicket in six overs. Shedge was out for 10 and conceded 23 runs without taking a wicket in two overs. Overall, Shedge scored 49 runs in four matches at 24.50 and took three wickets in four matches at 42.00. Eight teams have made it to the Super League, which will begin on November 30. Mumbai have been placed in Super League B (Group 2) alongside Rajasthan, Punjab and Andhra. Mumbai will play their opening match against Andhra at the Civil Lines Stadium in Nagpur on November 30, from 1:30 pm. On December 2, the 2022 and 2024-25 champions will next take on Punjab at the Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium in Jamtha from 4:30 pm. On December 4, Mumbai will play their final match of the Super League against Rajasthan at the VCA Stadium in Civil Lines from 1:30 pm. There will be no semi-finals in the Super League, with the group toppers clashing in the final on December 6.

item.description: The Arizona Diamondbacks are doing some Black Friday shopping today. The team acquired catcher Henry Davis from the Pittsburgh Pirates. item.description: Japan have beaten Wales twice but never in matches outside of their own country [Getty Images] It is not the traditional ending to a Wales rugby autumn campaign. After the euphoria and then disappointment of two epic international weekends in Cardiff, Wales face the prospect of finishing a November series in south west London with a fixture against Japan. It sounds unusual because the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship is exactly that. The concept of a finals weekend in one venue with six games over three days is laudable, but trying to get Welsh fans excited about defeating Japan to finish ninth rather than 10th in a 12-team tournament at a neutral ground is a tough sell, especially when you compare it to what happened in Cardiff two weeks ago. This autumn will always be remembered as the campaign where Wales shocked the rugby world by beating New Zealand for the first time since 1953 . Either side of that momentous day, there has been a lacklustre 28-21 defeat of Japan and a narrow 29-26 loss against Australia in a game Wales could and maybe should have won. Those exciting occasions in Cardiff will now be followed by a trip to Twickenham to take on Eddie Jones' Japan. It takes some getting used to. Wales face double-header dilemma It will be a strange experience with Wales facing Japan on a Saturday afternoon before England play New Zealand for third place. Is it a double-header or will Wales be providing the curtain-raiser to the main event? Whichever way you view the occasion, Wales head coach Steve Tandy knows his side will have to provide their own atmosphere with a sparse crowd present for Friday afternoon's match between Italy and Fiji before Ireland took on Australia in the evening. "We've spoken about it all week," said Tandy. "There's also a 40-minute bus trip which is not normal either because we usually stay closer. "We have also spoken about it being an early kick-off. "There might be people walking in while the game is going on, the crowd might fill up as the game goes on, so there's all these little things to consider.” Tandy says the squad know Twickenham will not match the intensity of Cardiff's Principality Stadium during the past couple of weeks. "It is a different type of atmosphere for us after three massive games at home and being unbelievably well supported," said Tandy. "We've got to adapt a different sort of mindset and create that energy on the field for ourselves." item.title: NFL insider: Brock Purdy's status 'up in the air' for 49ers-Seahawks
item.description: Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates the 35-10 win against the Minnesota Vikings at Estadio Banorte on Nov. 22, 2026, in Mexico City. (Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) As the San Francisco 49ers prepare for a pivotal showdown with their division rival Seahawks, it's still unclear whether Brock Purdy will play on Sunday. Purdy, who is in the midst of an MVP-caliber season, has missed the past two days of practice with an ankle sprain that occurred during last week's dominant win over the Vikings. And according to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, Purdy's status for Sunday is still "up in the air" as the Niners get back to the facility after Thanksgiving. On Friday's NFL Network " Good Morning Football " show, Rapoport said Purdy's injury has flown "under the radar," in part because he played through it and looked brilliant against Minnesota in Mexico City last week. In fact, some of Purdy's 49ers teammates didn't even realize he got hurt during the game because he kept on playing. But now that he's missed both practices on Wednesday and Thursday, his teammates are surely aware. Head coach Kyle Shanahan specified on Wednesday that Purdy doesn't have a high ankle sprain, which would knock him out for multiple weeks, but acknowledged it's possible that Purdy misses Sunday's game. Backup Mac Jones has been taking all of the reps in Purdy's place ahead of Friday's final 49ers practice, which Rapoport said will be pivotal. "If he, obviously, does not practice today, then doesn't bode well for him playing," he said. "If he is out there later today, probably going to make the start." We might not even need to wait until Sunday to find out for certain, either. Starting quarterbacks are effectively required to hold one interview session with reporters during the middle of the week before games. If the starter is ruled out, then the backup takes that spot. Purdy usually has his media session on Thursdays, but because of Thanksgiving, this week's presser was pushed to Friday. Purdy speaking on Friday won't immediately mean he's ruled out - after all, he spoke to reporters before the Rams game in Week 5 last year, but then didn't play in that game or in the following five games - but if it's Jones up there, that'll be a clear sign about what is set to happen on Sunday. Because the Bears beat the Lions to kick off a wild Thanksgiving slate, the 49ers need to beat the Seahawks to stay in the No. 1 spot in the NFC. Kickoff is set for Sunday at 1:25 p.m. on Fox. item.title: Tom Brady Rips Aaron Rodgers for Violating the ‘Sanctity’ of the Locker Room
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now During the Eagles-Cowboys game on Thanksgiving, Fox’s Tom Brady criticized Aaron Rodgers for violating the “ sanctity ” of the locker room. “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room,” Brady said. “You’re fighting with your teammates; you’re fighting with your coaches; you’re always acting as a team, together. [It] shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say.” Brady recognized that Rodgers is an all-time great, but believes it should always be about the team first. “It has nothing to do with his play style,” Brady said. “I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate, to me, was you cared about your teammates and your coaches, and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish. That supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote.” “Again, I was very fortunate. I was in a great locker room. I played for my teammates; I played for my coaches. There’s … nobody wins when the family feuds,” Brady added. The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place. We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. "The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place" Tom Brady takes issue with how Aaron Rodgers handled his Steelers benching on Wednesday pic.twitter.com/gRRpgcKo41 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 27, 2026 Rodgers was benched and ultimately released after he set an ultimatum to Mike McCarthy over offensive play-calling. Rodgers demanded his release if changes weren’t made. Rodgers revealed on The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday that it was contentious during his last conversation with McCarthy. Rodgers told McCarthy that he thought it was in the best interest of the team for somebody else to call plays and if not, they should release him. Rodgers also claimed that McCarthy falls asleep during meetings and snores, and just flat-out misses meetings, and he doesn’t care to get to know the defensive players. So what was the breaking point for Rodgers? He said McCarthy saying “1-2-3 Packers” at halftime of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles was the final straw. Rodgers said he doesn’t care about being released. That’s why he spoke up. “The truth is the truth,” he said. item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim end winless run with convincing victory over Nürnberg Frank Schmidt’s side made the perfect start when Patrick Mainka headed home from a corner in the 13th minute. However, Nürnberg restored parity shortly before half-time through a Marcel Costly own goal, setting up an intriguing second half. The visitors started the second period brightly, with Julian Justvan striking the post in the 49th minute after being teed up by William Bøving. Justvan also went close from distance later in the half, rattling the crossbar as Nürnberg searched for a breakthrough. Despite that promising spell, Heidenheim regained control of the contest and restored their advantage in the 61st minute. Following a Nürnberg throw-in that the visitors failed to clear, Tim Siersleben laid the ball back to Budu Zivzivadze, whose effort took a significant deflection off Fynn Otto before finding the net. The goal was subsequently allowed to stand following a VAR review for a possible offside. Heidenheim quickly added a third to put themselves firmly in the driving seat. In the 65th minute, Jan Schöppner initially saw his header from a Paul Hennrich cross saved by Jan Reichert, but the midfielder reacted quickest to convert the rebound from close range. Nürnberg attempted to find a route back into the game, with Justvan particularly unfortunate to see another effort strike the woodwork. The visitors were also denied when a mishit cross from Porstner struck the upright in the 81st minute. Heidenheim remained defensively organised during the closing stages, with Sirlord Conteh also seeing an effort blocked by Alexios Kalogeropoulos after being played into the penalty area by Alessandro Vogt. Four minutes of additional time offered Nürnberg little opportunity to mount a comeback, as Heidenheim comfortably saw out the remainder of the contest. The victory represents an important result for Schmidt’s side, who had gone seven consecutive league matches without winning. All three of their goals came from set-pieces, highlighting the effectiveness of their delivery and aerial threat. For Nürnberg and head coach Miroslav Klose, meanwhile, it is a second consecutive defeat after last weekend’s 2-1 home loss against Eintracht Braunschweig. Despite creating several opportunities, the visitors were ultimately made to pay for their defensive shortcomings and inability to take advantage of their second-half pressure.

(Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images) There are essentially two scenarios for Alabama, one much more likely than the other, but neither particularly probable. Alabama needs three things to happen this weekend in the more likely possibility: Alabama beats Auburn. Texas A&M beats Texas. Vanderbilt beats Tennessee. That’s because both Texas and Tennessee hold tiebreakers for having beaten Alabama, so since they enter the weekend with tied records in SEC play, Alabama needs to one-up them this weekend. However, there’s another scenario: a three-way tie. In a three-way tie, head-to-head can’t be used as the main tiebreaker, and CBS Sports revealed that the SEC would come down to its fourth tiebreaker, the cumulative SEC winning percentage of each of the three-way tied team’s conference opponents. If all three of Alabama, Texas and Tennessee win this weekend, Alabama can make the SEC title game if: Mississippi State beats Ole Miss. LSU beats Arkansas. item.title: Klinsmann defends comments by Hoeness, Rummenigge about Musiala
item.description: FILE PHOTO — Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala in action during the UEFA Champions League group stage soccer match between Lille and Bayern Munich at Stade Pierre-Mauroy. (is associated with: «Klinsmann defends comments by Hoeness, Rummenigge about Musiala») Sven Hoppe/dpa Former Germany national trainer Jürgen Klinsmann came out in defence of comments made by Bayern Munich bosses Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge over the health of international attacker Jamal Musiala on Friday. "I think this is also kind of a bit of German culture. We're known for going straight in the face of people and we just say something we feel in that moment," the former Bayern coach told US sports channel ESPN. "We don't actually mean it in a mean" way, he added. Musiala made his comeback last week from a torn muscle fibre that sidelined him for one and a half months, but suffered yet another setback. He was sidelined on Friday until further notice due to a muscle injury in his right thigh. The player has struggled with fitness since he broke his fibula during the Club World Cup in 2025. Besides that, Musiala revealed earlier this year that he suffers from absence seizures. His health condition sparked debate after Bayern supervisory board members Hoeness and Rummenigge raised the prospect of the midfielder taking a pay cut because of his health problems. The suggestion was widely slammed, including by Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich and former Bayern board member Oliver Kahn. The two also publicly questioned whether Musiala, one of Bayern's top earners with a contract running until 2030, could return to his previous level of performance. But of the controversial comments made, Klinsmann said the aim was actually "to bring up the topic and have an open eye-to-eye discussion and make both parties understand." Abroad, this might be perceived differently, he said. "But this is the way sometimes we communicate ... It's also a little bit in our DNA," Klinsmann said. 'They don't mean any harm to Musiala' "Sometimes, I think these comments are given a dynamic then," he said. "I don't think that Uli Hoeness or Karl-Heinz Rummenigge want to damage him in any way," said Klinsmann. "Maybe inside they are a bit frustrated, have concerns. But they don't mean any harm to Jamal Musiala." Klinsmann recalled his playing days at FC Bayern, "when we'd sometimes have fights in the locker room, verbally, face to face, where we just needed to get it out. Sometimes not really nice words but we got it out and we felt better about it afterwards." For Musiala, this is currently "a very, very difficult period of his career. It's an illness that's very difficult to deal with. We all hope for him that he'll get better and better step by step and is 100% again," said Klinsmann
